speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you are experiencing episodes of dizziness and vertigo. To help me understand your condition better, can you describe exactly what these episodes feel like and how long they last?

speaker: Patient
text: 70-year-old woman. The patient presents with sudden episodes of dizziness that are position dependent. She describes experiencing a false sensation of motion and occasional spinning, indicative of vertigo. She denies any recent illnesses, injuries, or significant changes in health status, apart from age-related hearing loss (presbycusis).

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. The fact that your dizziness is position-dependent and feels like spinning is very specific. Does this spinning sensation occur when you roll over in bed, tilt your head back, or bend down?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Episodes of dizziness and spinning sensation. I also have Position dependent vertigo, No recent illness, No hearing loss besides presbycusis.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV)

The history of position-dependent spinning in an elderly patient with presbycusis is classic for BPPV. To confirm the diagnosis, do you have access to a Dix-Hallpike test result or any prior head imaging?
